addendum: Independent review of A19 Theorems A, B, H (seat M2a worker and cold reader, seat M2a-v verifier, both Opus, neither saw A19's verdicts). A: confirmed (matches R-113 O1). B: confirmed; any r >= 2 suffices; exact form sum over v_p(z) = 1 of a_z (z/p) == u mod pO. H: confirmed with wording fixes: (1) add O cap Q = Z (p^k O meets Z in p^k Z); (2) state D_k explicitly: prime values p^v u_q, modulus p^(v+k), value at 1 free; (3) v is free (chosen with the construction); with v fixed the minimal degrees change (computed: v = 1 gives only k = 1 at p = 2, k <= 2 at p = 3). Formulas hold for signed degree and for total factor count. Computed: Z_signed = S(p^ceil(k/2)), Z_cheap = S(p^k) by two independent methods (elimination mod p^N with v <= 8; Hermite normal form over Z with every offset), p = 2 (k <= 8), 3 (k <= 6), 5 (k <= 5), 7 (k <= 4); constructions pass on every n <= 2 * 10^5 (six cases, negative controls fail).

Verifier's derivation, not yet cold-read: a one-way slice reduction maps a mu identity at levels 0..L (R-053) to a cheap D_k solution with nodes 1..L+1 and v = v_p(lcm(1..L+1)), so H's lower bound gives L >= S(p^k) - 1 (R-053's lower bound) in three lines; Z_cheap = L + 1. The converse fails (mu allows only E_p corrections, v = 0), so the constructions are different statements. Computed agreement p = 2 (k <= 5), 3 (k <= 3), 5 (k <= 2).

Independent review of A19 Theorems D, E, J, K, G (seat M2c worker and cold reader, seat M2c-v verifier, both Opus). G (Lelechenko arXiv:1305.1639v3 Theorem 5 gap): confirmed. Proof of Theorem 5, page 9: the bound x^{b/k2 + (1 - b k1/k2) c/k1} uses sum_{d<=U} d^{-b k1/k2} << U^{1 - b k1/k2}, false when b k1 > k2. Counterexample mu (k1 = 3, a = 2/3) with d_3 (k2 = 1, b = 3/5): printed 9/23, true first-sum exponent 3/5. Safe bound max(a/k1, b/k2, T): 3/5, or 5/9 with b = 5/9 (printed 17/45); in both cases this is also the best over c for that scheme. New: the paper's Example 14 (claimed 5/9) is in the same gap regime; the proof supports 2/3. Lelechenko's Theorem 2 (7/15 parity) stands (Example 13 is in the valid regime). This is a gap in the proof, not a disproof of the statement.

D: confirmed pointwise and summed (n, x <= 10^5; independent rebuild n <= 2 * 10^4). Refutation of our Q2 conjectures confirmed with qualification: Q2.3 (mod 2 list) refuted as a literal list; Q2.2 (mod 3, d_3-type up to a twist w == 1 mod 3) refuted literally (shifts 0, 2, 4; F(3^e) = 273), but for q != 3 the local factor is == (1 - t)^3 mod 3, so the spirit survives; restate before calling it dead. E: confirmed with fix: the modulus M must include p^m = 9. J: confirmed for theta-only linear filters (scope as stated; filters mixing F components not covered); 4,143 nonprincipal pairs to 10^5 reproduced twice, once with no theta counts. K: confirmed with fix: the argument is modulus-independent (S3 field Q(cuberoot 2, sqrt(-3)), Chebotarev); M must include 2^m; witnesses for M = 2^m * 315 recorded in m2/cv/REPORT_M2cv.md. Section 7 ternary identity (F1): every x <= 10^5 by seat M2c; F1(10^6) = 106,030,594 agrees with the director's independent sieve value in the A25 addendum. Its x^(5/9) cost claim was not tested.

Cold read of the mu to cheap D_k reduction (supersedes 'not yet cold-read'): HOLDS WITH FIXES. Write b_w = c_{w-1} on nodes w in 1..L+1; cite H's moment lemma (H3)-(H4) rather than the full-function Theorem H (H8 gives a full lift); the slice condition 'primes 1 mod M' is not needed (any squarefree n). Direct form without D: Q(t) = prod (t - w) over the active nodes gives p^k | q_0 | (L+1)!, so L + 1 >= S(p^k). Computed: thresholds exactly L = S(p^k) - 1 for p = 2 (k <= 3), p = 3 (k <= 2). Converse remark not checked in depth.

addendum: Independent review of A19 Results M, N, section 9 and Theorem L (seat M2d worker and cold reader, seat M2d-v verifier, both Opus). Result M (pi(x) mod 3 below square-root time iff D_3(x) mod 9 below square-root time): confirmed both directions, run as literal oracle algorithms (all x <= 10^5; both seats' own code), at 10^8, 10^9 + 7, 3^19, 10^10, 10^11 with independent pi; cost: forward x^(1/3) oracle calls, reverse x^(1/3) log x; a fixed power saving below 1/2 survives both ways. Wording fix: 'at least two' distinct prime factors. Result N: confirmed (identities to 10^5; c_L == mu mod 3 first fails at 2^(3^L)). Theorem L: confirmed (disc -108, conductor 6, class number 3; identities mod 8 and parity for every n, x <= 10^5); cost x^(1+o(1)) as an upper bound. Section 9: identities and exponent arithmetic unconditional; x^(5/11) parity needs D_2 in y^(1/3+o(1)) and (second route) HKM Theorem 5 (not checked here); 47/104 conditional on Li (unreviewed); 9c per-shell bounds rest on Sladkey's semi-formal G argument.

x^(5/9) frontier for D_3 (A19 section 7 cost claim): GAP in the source, closed by our fix (cost bound measured, proof pending). Sladkey (arXiv:1206.3369) gives no procedure for the incomplete sum S(n, x1, sqrt n) with arbitrary x1 (his 'partial result' holds only for x1 <= x_min, about z <= n^(1/4)); the naive finish costs Theta(x^(2/3)) (measured 0.049 x^(2/3)). Fix (seat M2d-v): exact axis swap sum_{a<=b<=r} floor(y/b) = sum_{a<=b<=c} floor(y/b) + r(r-c) + sum_{r<t<=M} floor(y/t) - c(M-r), r = isqrt(y), c = min(max(a-1, floor(y^(1/3))), r), M = floor(y/(c+1)), with a Stern-Brocot hull walk for the last sum. Correct on 129,022 cases against brute force (all N <= 3000, random to 10^12, special N, N to 10^14); D_3 by (F1) matches sieves and an independent route to 10^10. Cost per call about y^(1/3) log y uniformly in the lower limit (measured to 10^18); total (F1) cost 16.0 to 22.3 times x^(5/9) from 10^9 to 10^19 (fitted slope 0.566, 0.537 after dividing by ln x). pi(x) mod 3 via Result M with this oracle correct at 10^9 + 7, 10^10, 10^11 (pi(10^11) = 4,118,054,813, residue 2). Rigorous substitute in the literature: Polymath section 2.1 block method (sketch). Other published: Lelechenko Theorem 3 gives D_3 in x^(3/5+eps) (valid regime).
